title: SRE weekly orbit briefing — oncall orchestration & incident synthesis
content:
Context and purpose:
This doc is the weekly SRE briefing ("orbit") focused on on-call orchestration, a short synthesis of incidents from the last 7 days, SLO health signals, and explicit handoff notes for next shifts. Treat as the single source for what to escalate and what to follow up in the next sprint.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Two medium-severity incidents this week: an autoscaler undercount (Jun 5) and a KV-cache cold-start storm (Jun 6). Both impacted 99th p50 latencies for hosted API routes (text-generation) and triggered routed-fallbacks for Dedicated customers.
- SLO snapshot: request latency (p99) breached target twice; error budget consumption up ~1.9% this week. No customer-facing SLA credit expected but keep monitoring.
- Immediate action items created and owners assigned; see action list below.

Incident A — autoscaler undercount (2027-06-05 03:10 UTC)
- Summary: HorizontalAutoscaler svc under-counted active pods when burst allocations came from colocated private deployments. Autoscaler reported available capacity ~30% lower than actual; control-plane delayed scale-up by ~120s causing queueing and spike in generation latency.
- Impact: 03:10–03:14 UTC: p99 generation latency on hosted-api-route /v1/generate rose from 420ms -> 1.6s, 500s spiked for a small subset of requests that hit KV misses. No persistent data loss; some Dedicated customers saw degraded tail latency and temporary routed-fallback to smaller model variants.
- Detection: Alert: autoscaler-scale-delay > 90s (pager). Oncall paged at 03:12.
- Root cause hypothesis: race in the scale decision path when API server receives simultaneous burst from multiple zones; metric aggregator timestamps were misaligned causing the HPA evaluation window to drop recent pod readiness events.
- Mitigation steps taken: manually triggered scale-up, rolled a hotfix to aggregator config to increase evaluation window (temp), and activated region-fallback policy for affected tenants.
- Permanent fixes planned: SRE-482 (Jira) — increase aggregator time-window + add ingest-order checks; SRE-489 — add synthetic canary to validate HPA decisions during bursts.

Incident B — KV-cache cold-start storm (2027-06-06 21:40 UTC)
- Summary: After a routine deploy that changed cache sharding logic, a fraction of replica pods warmed cold, leading to a cascade of KV misses. Cache warm-up traffic pattern created sustained CPU pressure on transformer kernels initiating autoscale churn.
- Impact: 21:40–22:05 UTC: sustained elevated latency p95-> p99 with transient 429s observed when local request queues overflowed. A small set of customers saw degraded generation quality due to fallback quantized model used during overload.
- Detection: Observability spike on KV-miss-rate alert; first page at 21:44.
- Root cause: sharding change caused uneven prefix mapping; warmup traffic concentrated on 2/8 shards.
- Mitigation: rollback of the sharding change to previous mapping, manual re-warm of caches, and temporary throttling of non-critical eval traffic.
- Follow ups: add rollout-step to force staggered cache warmups in deployment pipeline; create automated shard-distribution check in CI.

SLOs and metrics (end-to-end):
- p99 latency SLO (text-generation, hosted): target 800ms. Observed breach windows: Jun 5 (03:10–03:20), Jun 6 (21:40–22:10).
- Error budget status: starting week: 98.6% remaining; post incidents: 96.7% remaining.
- New monitoring change: adding p95->p99 delta alert to catch steep tail jumps before absolute p99 breach. See PR linked above.

On-call handoff notes (incoming shift):
- Current state: autoscaler hotfix is in place (config change only, reversible). Aggregator window set to +45s temporarily. KV sharding rollback completed and stable.
- What to watch first 4h:
  * autoscaler-scale-delay alert (pager) — if it fires again, escalate to runtime team and consider global policy soft-limit to prevent further queue spikes
  * kv-miss-rate (region us-west1) — check top prefixes and CPU per-pod; if >70% CPU and miss-rate rising, enable throttle for evaluation traffic
  * routed-fallback events — track per-tenant fallbacks and owner contact list in Slack (linked below)
- Contact list: runtime@redwood (pager duty), infra-leads: Luca Ramirez, Taylor Nguyen (work hours), oncall-ops: Jordan Blake (backup)
- Runbooks to follow: runbook/autoscaler-eval, runbook/cache-warmup, runbook/model-fallbacks (links in linked_artifacts).

Action items and owners (short):
- SRE-482 (Priya) — finalize aggregator ingest-order guards and add unit tests; due 2027-06-14
- SRE-489 (Luca) — implement synthetic HPA canary and add to CI; due 2027-06-21
- ENG-Runtime-1182 (Taylor) — add p95->p99 delta alert, add dashboard panel for warmup heatmap; due 2027-06-10
- OPS-heatmap (Jordan) — create a periodic report of shard distribution and top prefixes, email weekly to runtime and SRE; due 2027-06-11

Meeting notes (weekly stability sync — 2027-06-07 10:00 UTC):
- Attendance: Priya, Luca, Taylor, Jordan, product-observability rep (Anya).
- Topics and outcomes:
  * Incident postmortem plan: short postmortem for autoscaler incident; Priya to lead, include timeline and mitigation details, target publish 2027-06-12.
  * Rollout policy update: decided to require staggered cache warmup for any change touching cache sharding or placement. Taylor to add a pipeline gate.
  * SLA communication: product wants a short note summarizing impact for affected customers — Jordan to draft and run through legal.
  * Long-term: evaluate replacing time-window based HPA with event-ordered evaluations (research spike).

Notes to next rotation / sticky items:
- Do not revert autoscaler window change unless you confirm synthetic canary is green. Revert only with runtime lead approval.
- If you see repeated routed-fallbacks for the same tenant, open a dedicated incident channel and contact solutions-eng for customer communications.
- Keep an eye on the new p95->p99 delta signal; tune threshold after 48h of data.

Appendix (quick links):
- Jira: SRE-482, SRE-489
- GitHub PR: runtime/pull/1182
- Slack thread: #sre-bridge-thread-2027-06-05
- Runbooks: runbook/autoscaler-eval, runbook/cache-warmup, runbook/model-fallbacks

Prepared by: Priya Menon (eng-sre). Reviewed by: Luca Ramirez, Taylor Nguyen.

-- end of briefing --
